title: Why We Dream
passages: Every night, while your body rests, your brain stays busy. Many people who study sleep think dreams may help us sort through the day. The brain seems to replay MEMORIES, keep the useful ones, and let others fade, a little like tidying a messy room. Some think dreams let us REHEARSE facing our fears in a safe place. Others believe dreams help us solve problems, which may be why an answer sometimes appears after a good night of sleep. No one knows for sure, and that puzzle is part of what makes dreams so interesting.

Dreams can feel strange and VIVID. You might fly over rooftops, talk with an old friend, or find a door that was never there. Some dreams are joyful, and some are scary enough to wake you up. Often a dream feels completely real until the moment you open your eyes. People all over the world have wondered about these night stories. In some cultures, families share their dreams at breakfast and talk about what they might mean. Others see dreams as messages from ANCESTORS or as a way to glimpse the future. Each idea shows how much people care about the hidden life of the sleeping mind.
